newsitem.title: USA: O.J. Simpson criminal case lawyer sanctioned.
newsitem.headline: O.J. Simpson criminal case lawyer sanctioned.

text.p: The California State Bar sanctioned one of O.J. Simpson's defence attorneys and is expected to sanction another, an official said Friday.
In addition, a third lawyer marginally involved in the former football star's criminal trial received a written caution, Judy Johnson, the bar's chief trial counsel, said.

Defence attorney Carl Douglas was sanctioned for allegedly misusing his subpoena powers, Johnson said, while Barry Scheck, a New York attorney specialising in DNA evidence, faces disciplinary action for allegedly practicing law in California without a valid licence during part of the trial.

The bar also issued a warning letter to Robert Tourtelot, a Los Angeles lawyer who represented then-Los Angeles detective Mark Fuhrman, a disgraced prosecution witness, in civil suits. The letter to Tourtelot, which does not constitute a formal disciplinary action, was issued because the attorney made public comments "perceived as potentially harmful" to his former client, Johnson said.

Fuhrman, who testified during Simpson's trial to finding a bloody glove on the sports star's estate, later pleaded no contest to a single charge of perjury arising from his denial on the witness stand that he had frequently used the word "nigger," and was fined and placed on probation.

Simpson was acquitted of the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman, by a criminal court jury in October 1995. But he was found liable for their deaths by a civil court jury this year and ordered to pay the families of the victims more than $30 million in damages.
The California bar said it received hundreds of complaints from the public and members of the bar about the conduct of attorneys involved in the televised criminal trial.

Johnson said the bar investigated 10 lawyers involved in the Simpson case over a 16-month period. Bar spokeswoman Jaclyn Reinhardt said one other attorney, whom she did not identify, remained under investigation.

On Thursday, State Bar Court Judge Carlos Velarde issued a formal public reproval against Douglas. Velarde also offered to issue a public reproval to Scheck. If he fails to accept the offer, formal charges will be filed in State Bar Court, Johnson said.

A public reproval -- a censure that leaves a permanent mark on an attorney's record -- is one of the many disciplinary actions that may be imposed on lawyers who violate the bar's rules of professional conduct.
The bar alleged that Douglas, who accepted the sanction, allowed subpoenas to be issued illegally under his name. The witnesses named in the subpoenas did not testify in the trial.
Scheck faces disciplinary action because he was an inactive member of the California bar during the first eight months of the year-long trial, Johnson said.
